what_matters.tag_note: Super Micro · after Tuesday's US close
what_matters.head: After Tuesday's US close, Super Micro raised its estimate of last quarter's revenue to $18.5–19.5B, from its forecast of $14.5–15.5B, citing demand for AI platforms.
what_matters.detail: It put gross margin at 12.0–12.5%, above its 10.4–10.8% forecast; the figures are preliminary, with full results on 3 Nov. Its shares rose about 12% after hours. Samsung and SK Hynix rose about 5% in Seoul by 12:07 SGT, and Yahoo Finance tied the Asian chip rally to the update. Nasdaq 100 futures were up 1% in Asian trading. Not in Tuesday's US prices.

what_matters.head: Meta reports after the New York close tonight, the first of Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon to report since last week's chip and software sell-off.
what_matters.detail: Analysts expect revenue of about $63.4B (range $61.7–65.3B, 49 analysts) and earnings per share of about $5.54, against the company's forecast of $61–64B. Meta's 2026 spending plan for data centres and equipment is $130–145B. The quarter carries a legal charge of about $10B that Meta said was not in its expense forecast.

what_matters.head: Nokia reports at about 13:00 SGT tomorrow, and Bloom Energy after the New York close on Thursday (about 04:05 SGT Friday).
what_matters.detail: Lam Research, not held, is expected after the New York close on Thursday too; its results bear on ASML, Micron, SK Hynix and Sandisk. Western Digital, also not held, follows early Saturday SGT.

latest.tape_note: US stocks were mixed on Tuesday: the Dow rose 1.0% and the S&P 500 0.3%, while the Nasdaq ended flat. Health-care stocks led, and Equifax, Hasbro and 3M rose after their results; General Motors fell 6.8% on its profit forecast (Investing.com). The chip fund slipped 0.4%, after a 1.7% rise on Monday that ended its nine-session losing run. Brent crude fell more than 2% during the day after a report that Qatar and Pakistan had proposed a middle-ground plan for the US and Iran, then recovered after Iran's first vice president spoke of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz (Investing.com); US crude settled 1.8% lower. The 10-year Treasury yield ended at 5.12%.
latest.tonight: Nvidia's GTC Berlin keynote at 17:00 SGT today. Meta's results at about 04:05 SGT Thursday (call 04:30). Nothing on the economic calendar. Thursday: Micron's Taichung union mediation, and Nokia's results at about 13:00 SGT.

recent.headline: After Tuesday's US close, Super Micro raised its estimate of last quarter's revenue to $18.5–19.5B, from its forecast of $14.5–15.5B, citing demand for AI platforms.
Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.

Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
MAS left its Singapore-dollar policy unchanged this morning. All 10 analysts in a Reuters poll last week had expected it to tighten again, after a very slight tightening in July.
